target: Both office-chair wheel/base assemblies are separated from the reconstructed floor rather than contacting it.

hints.E1: Carefully compare the reference image, current render, and existing scene. Identify and fix important discrepancies, and check whether your changes actually improve the reconstruction or introduce other problems.
hints.E2: Both chairs' wheel/base assemblies sit above the reconstructed floor rather than making floor contact.
hints.E3:
Both chairs' wheel/base assemblies sit above the reconstructed floor rather than making floor contact.

Treat each chair as a connected assembly and inspect the evaluated lowest wheel surfaces against the floor directly beneath them. If the internal connections are sound, align the assembly to the support surface, then verify each caster in a side view and check that the seat, post and spokes remain connected without floor penetration.
hints.E4:
Both chairs' wheel/base assemblies sit above the reconstructed floor rather than making floor contact.

Implement and compare two candidates: align each whole chair assembly to its local floor, or revise caster orientation and geometry while retaining the body height. Use evaluated geometry and side views to test contact for every wheel on both chairs, not just overlapping bounding boxes; compare the camera-view caster silhouette with the reference. Check for floor penetration, broken wheel-to-spoke or post-to-seat connections, and changes in seat clearance. Choose based on those observations rather than assuming either cause is established.
